_note: Per-trimester recommended/limit/avoid foods with reasons. Conservative, widely-accepted guidance — see README for which items are flagged review:true.
disclaimer: This guide is general information, not medical advice. Always follow your own doctor's or dietitian's guidance for your pregnancy.

items.reason: No amount of alcohol is known to be safe during pregnancy.

items.item: Raw or undercooked meat, poultry, eggs, and seafood
items.reason: Risk of harmful bacteria and parasites, such as Listeria, Salmonella, and Toxoplasma.

items.item: Unpasteurized milk, juice, and soft cheeses (like brie or feta) made from it
items.reason: Can carry Listeria and other harmful bacteria.

items.item: High-mercury fish (shark, swordfish, king mackerel, tilefish, bigeye tuna)
items.reason: Mercury can harm your baby's developing nervous system.

items.item: Raw sprouts (alfalfa, clover, radish, mung bean)
items.reason: Bacteria can get inside the sprout where washing can't reach it.

items.item: Deli meats and smoked seafood, unless heated until steaming hot
items.reason: Risk of Listeria, which survives refrigeration but not high heat.
Risk of bacteria and pesticide residue on the skin.

recommended.item: Folate-rich foods — leafy greens, lentils, beans, fortified cereal
recommended.reason: Folate helps prevent neural tube defects during this early, critical stage of development.
Many people find ginger helps settle morning sickness, though how well it works varies.
recommended.review_note: Evidence and recommended amounts for ginger vary by source — worth a quick check with her doctor, especially if nausea is severe.

recommended.reason: Can be gentler on the stomach if nausea is an issue.
Keeping something in the stomach often helps with nausea more than a few large meals.

limit.reason: Most guidelines suggest staying under about 200mg a day (roughly one 12oz cup of coffee).
limit.review_note: The exact safe caffeine limit varies a little between guidelines — confirm the number her doctor is comfortable with.

recommended.item: Iron-rich foods — lean meat, beans, spinach, fortified cereal
recommended.reason: Supports the big increase in blood volume and helps prevent anemia.

recommended.item: Calcium-rich foods — dairy, fortified plant milk, tofu, leafy greens
recommended.reason: Supports your baby's developing bones and teeth.

recommended.item: Vitamin C rich foods — citrus fruit, bell peppers, tomatoes
recommended.reason: Helps your body absorb iron from food more effectively.

recommended.item: Protein — eggs, beans, fish, poultry, dairy
recommended.reason: Supports your baby's rapid growth during this stage.

limit.reason: Keep following the same rough limit as trimester 1 — about 200mg a day.
limit.review_note: Same caffeine note as trimester 1 — confirm the number with her doctor.

limit.item: Low-mercury fish (salmon, shrimp, tilapia, canned light tuna)
limit.reason: A good source of omega-3s, but most guidelines suggest about 2-3 servings a week to limit mercury exposure.
limit.review_note: Weekly fish serving limits vary a bit by country/guideline — good to confirm the number with her doctor.

recommended.item: Fiber-rich foods — whole grains, fruits, vegetables, beans
recommended.reason: Helps with constipation, which is common as the growing baby puts pressure on the digestive system.
Can ease heartburn and the feeling of fullness as there's less room for the stomach to expand.

recommended.item: Continued iron and calcium rich foods
recommended.reason: Needs for both stay high as your baby puts on weight quickly in the final weeks.
Supports healthy amniotic fluid levels and can help reduce swelling.

limit.reason: Keep following the same rough limit as earlier — about 200mg a day.
limit.review_note: Same caffeine note as earlier trimesters — confirm the number with her doctor.

limit.reason: May contribute to extra swelling for some people late in pregnancy.
